extracted.intended_audience: economists, policymakers, researchers and students interested in Quebec regional economy, trade and labour-market analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Analytic research report profiling Quebec's employment, trade and economic impacts (primarily 1970s–1989), with descriptive statistics, sectoral/trade tables and five candidate explanations for the deterioration in employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taux de chômage (unemployment rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of the labour force without a job but actively seeking work (9.3% for Quebec in 1989 as reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined per the monthly Labour Force Survey; the text flags ambiguity (flows between inactivity/activity and varying intensity of job search) and cautions not to rely on this measure alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taux d'activité (labour force participation rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of the working-age population classified as active on the labour market (e.g., 64% in Quebec in 1989).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to decompose differences in employment between provinces (part of the explanation for Quebec–Ontario employment gap).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapport emploi-population (employment–population ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number employed per 1,000 working-age persons (580 per 1,000 in Quebec in 1989); recommended as a complementary measure to the unemployment rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors advocate using this ratio as a less ambiguous measure of an economy’s capacity to put its population to work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emploi par tranche de 1 000 personnes (employment per 1,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute employment density in the working-age population (e.g., Quebec 580/1,000; Ontario 663/1,000 in 1989).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to quantify interprovincial employment deficits and to illustrate relative labour-market tightness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durée moyenne du chômage (average duration of unemployment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average spell length of unemployment (over 5 months in 1989; 30% of unemployed >6 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of persistence and potential hysteresis effects; used to distinguish short-term churn from chronic unemployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flux mensuels entre inactivité et activité (labour-market flows)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monthly movements of people between inactivity, employment and unemployment (example: in a month 40 unemployed leave and are replaced by 40 new unemployed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to emphasise the dynamic nature of unemployment and the importance of flow measures beside stock measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidence du travail à temps partiel involontaire (involuntary part-time incidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of workers in part-time employment who would prefer full-time work (noted as twice as high in Quebec compared with Ontario).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of underemployment and labour-market precariousness; supports conclusions about job quality as well as quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taux de chômage par niveau d'instruction (unemployment by education)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unemployment rates broken down by education level (e.g., 4.7% for university graduates vs. 13.1% for workers with less than grade 8 in 1989).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show differential vulnerability to cyclical changes and structural shifts in demand for skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts relatives dans les importations et exportations (shares of imports/exports)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional and sectoral shares of total imports and exports (many figures/tables show shares by region, sector, and commodity groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to map the geographic and sectoral composition of trade and identify dominant trading partners/industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taux de croissance annuel moyen des exportations (average annual export growth rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average annual growth rates for exports to specific US regions or by industry (tables list rates for 1976–1987 and other periods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to rank industries/regions by dynamism and to identify sectors with fastest/slowest export growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part des exportations québécoises vers régions US (export destination concentration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of Quebec exports destined for specific U.S. regions (tables include shares where a US region accounts for 75%+ of exports to that destination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to highlight concentration/vulnerability of export markets and to compute region-specific growth indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industries exportatrices et croissance sectorielle (industry export profiles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of principal exporting industries and their share/growth (e.g., vehicle parts, communications equipment, machinery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps diagnose which sectors drive exports and which lag; tables enumerate industries with highest and lowest export growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact économique (direct, indirect, total effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMPACT accounting of exports on Quebec measured in direct, indirect and total effects across categories: person-years of employment, wages, other gross incomes, value added, imports, and government revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables VI.1–VI.2 provide numerical decompositions; this is the principal framework for estimating the economic footprint of exports (gives both level and multiplier implications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composantes des effets économiques (labour, wages, value added, imports)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific categories used within impact accounting: main-d'oeuvre (person-years), salaires et gages avant impôts, autres revenus bruts, valeur ajoutée, importations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category is reported as direct/indirect/total; useful for assessing distributional and leakages (e.g., imports) associated with export activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenus du gouvernement (provincial and federal tax receipts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates of government revenues attributable to exports: taxes on wages, parafiscalité, indirect taxes, broken out by Quebec and federal levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported to show fiscal impacts of trade and to compare provincial vs federal fiscal benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratio international / interprovincial (comparative impact ratios)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratios comparing impacts of international exports to interprovincial exports across categories (employment, wages, value added, imports, government revenues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess whether international vs domestic trade generate different multipliers or fiscal outcomes (see Table VI.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commerce international des services (receipts/payments/balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics for cross-border services trade: receipts, payments and resulting balances by region and year (tables and figures for 1983–1985).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in conjunction with goods trade to provide a fuller picture of external accounts and sectoral composition (e.g., consulting services).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taux de couverture des livraisons / taux de couverture des biens/services
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage rate of deliveries or goods/services (figures show percentage coverage across regions/sectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphical metric used to compare domestic vs international market coverage and to identify surpluses/deficits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratio des exportations sur le PIB (exports/ GDP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of exports (domestic, international, total) relative to regional GDP (figures IV.4–IV.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare openness and export-dependence across provinces and over time (1974, 1979, 1984).

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldes commerciaux régionaux (trade balances by region/sector)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional trade surpluses or deficits by sector and overall (figures show balances for goods and services by province/region).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves to identify which provinces/sectors run deficits vs surpluses and to trace structural trade positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts relatives et indices sectoriels hors commodités (shares excluding certain commodities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shares and balances recalculated excluding cereals, other agricultural products, petroleum/coal and mineral fuels (used in several figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adjustment isolates manufactured and non-fuel trade to highlight structural industry patterns apart from commodity cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure industrielle de l'emploi (sectoral employment shares)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment distribution across primary, manufacturing, construction, tertiary sectors (e.g., primary 3.5% in 1989; tertiary ~70%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to characterise the economy’s sectoral profile and long-term trends (decline in non-durable manufacturing, rise in durable goods and services).

rubrics_metrics.name: Niveaux salariaux relatifs (wage level ratios)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average wage in Quebec relative to Ontario (e.g., 93% in 1972 rising to 102% in 1982 then falling back to 93% during the 1980s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employed to assess competitiveness and as an explanatory variable for employment changes (higher relative wages can depress employment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mesure synthétique de l'ouverture du régime d'assurance-chômage (UI generosity/openess metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthetic percentage measure of how much unemployment insurance can increase a worker’s annual income when qualifying (used to summarise reforms' generosity; rose with 1971 reform and later declined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an aggregate indicator of policy-induced labour-market incentives and to estimate its possible effect on unemployment incidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cinq hypothèses explicatives de la détérioration de l'emploi (evaluative criteria for causes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five candidate causes used to explain Quebec’s employment deterioration: (1) demographic congestion from baby-boom and female labour-force entry; (2) easier access to unemployment insurance; (3) wage push via construction decrees, public-sector collective agreements and minimum-wage regulation; (4) deep industrial structural mutations; (5) repeated monetary contractions to control inflation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are treated as evaluative criteria in the analytical part: each is examined for timing, magnitude and persistence to assess its contribution to employment decline across the 1970s and 1980s.
